question: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹4,000 at 7.5% per annum rate of interest deposited on 5 February 2024 and withdrawn on 6 April 2024.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total days = 24 (Feb) + 31 (Mar) + 6 (Apr) = 61 days.

Since 2024 is a leap year (366 days), time in years = 61 ÷ 366 = 1/6 year.

Simple Interest = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

SI = (4000 × 7.5 × 1/6) ÷ 100 = 50

**∴ The correct answer is ₹50.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹4000

Rate of Interest (R) = 7.5% per annum

Date of deposit = 5 February 2024

Date of withdrawal = 6 April 2024

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 
• 
 
 
 
 5 Feb 2024
 6 Apr 2024
 
 
 P = ₹4000
 
 
 A = ₹4050
 
 

 
 
 Time = 61 Days
 
 
 Rate = 7.5% p.a.
 SI = ₹50

**Calculations:**

⇒ Number of days in February (2024 is a leap year) = 29 − 5 = 24 days

⇒ Number of days in March = 31 days

⇒ Number of days in April = 6 days

⇒ Total duration = 24 + 31 + 6 = 61 days

⇒ Since 2024 has 366 days, Time (T) in years = 61 ÷ 366 = 1/6 year

⇒ SI = (4000 × 7.5 × 1) ÷ (100 × 6)

⇒ SI = 30000 ÷ 600

⇒ SI = 50

**∴ The correct answer is ₹50.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Counting Days for Interest

When calculating interest between two specific dates, generally only one of the boundary dates (either the deposit date or the withdrawal date) is counted, but never both.

Leap Year Calculation

A year perfectly divisible by 4 is a leap year containing 366 days. Always use 366 as the denominator when formulating the time portion in years if the calculated days include the 29th of February.

Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

In Simple Interest, the principal balance does not change throughout the entire lending period. Under Compound Interest, accumulated interest is added periodically back to the principal, forming a new base for subsequent calculations.
